In scripts/lib/verify-lib.mjs, readIndex (line 75) runs Number() directly on the attribute string. The selector &#39;[data-step-index]&#39; only matches an element that has the attribute, so an absent hook gives Number(undefined), which is NaN, and is rejected. But a blank or whitespace-only value is also non-numeric, and Number(&#39;&#39;) or Number(&#39; &#39;) is 0. That 0 passes the first-step check `if (initial !== 0)` at line 110, so step 1 is accepted on a non-numeric hook. Judge B&#39;s reason is borne out by these lines and decides this clause, so I rule B&#39;s fail. Judge A says &#39;Number(null) cannot arise&#39; because of the selector. That is true, but it only covers the absent-attribute case, not a blank one. Judge C says an absent hook gives NaN. Also true, but C does not address a blank or whitespace value, which the guidance&#39;s &#39;non-numeric&#39; clause covers. The other parts of the requirement are met: an unreadable or zero step count fails through `!(total &gt; 0)` at line 108; later steps must reach exactly index+1 (lines 119-130); and the e2e case &#39;a transition that does not advance the step index&#39; asserts FAIL render and &#39;step 5 of 9 (index 4)&#39;. It injected five verification faults (build, missing sample, console error, page error, stuck transition) and ran inspection diagnostics on collision, allowed-overlap and clean fixtures. The skill-conversation and scaffold-decision scenarios were not exercised. verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":2585,"end_line":2591,"lines":[{"line":2585,"text":"## Round 1 finding A-002: the inspection helper reported a settled first step whose scene text was missing"},{"line":2586,"text":"- **Question:** the tester reports two helper runs where `step-01.png` showed the `prompt` and `you` outlines without their text or icon, while the log said `step 1/9 ... settled` and `0 advisory warnings`. Is that a defect, and what is the cause?"},{"line":2587,"text":"- **Requirement:** `presentation-verification`, \"Visual inspection artifacts\" and \"Screenshots are settled\": the helper waits for transitions to settle before each screenshot. `presentation-skill`, \"Self-verify before reporting completion\": the visual check uses settled screenshots."},{"line":2588,"text":"- **Ruling:** the symptom could not be reproduced, but the helper's settled check was weaker than its claim, so I hardened it. Evidence for the first part: I ran the helper five times at the default 1500 ms settle, including three runs with every core busy, and every `step-01.png` was byte-identical (md5 `03e51f0b…`) and showed the text and icon. The tester's own preserved screenshots, `sample-wide-step-01-helper-default.png` and `sample-wide-step-01-helper-3000.png`, are byte-identical to that capture and also show the text and icon. The blank capture itself was not preserved. The old check only looked at the `Appear` and scene wrapper opacities, so it could not notice a first load whose entities were not yet painted, whatever the cause. Step 1 has no entry transition, which also explains why only the first capture was affected. I ruled this a real weakness in the \"settled\" claim, not a runtime defect: the sample renders its entities correctly."},{"line":2589,"text":"- **Change:** before each screenshot the helper now also waits for fonts to load, then takes two samples of every entity two animation frames and 100 ms apart. A step counts as settled only when no entity moved or resized by more than 0.5 px, faded, appeared or disappeared between the samples. It retries for up to 5 s. If it still is not settled, it prints the existing `UNSETTLED` line and a warning that names up to three affected entities. An entity that is steady but deliberately dimmed or hidden counts as settled, and elements sharing one entity id are keyed by DOM order so each is compared with itself. The helper script and its library were copied unchanged into the bootstrap template, so the parity contract still holds. The kit and the sample are untouched."},{"line":2590,"text":"- **Regression coverage:** new unit tests of `unsettledEntities` in `tests/unit/inspect-diagnostics.test.ts` (steady; moving, resizing, fading, appearing or disappearing entities; steady dimmed or hidden entities) and of `collectSceneContent` in `tests/unit/inspect-scene-content.test.ts` (duplicate ids, accumulated opacity). Output: `evidence/acceptance-fix-2-unit.log` and, after validator review changes, `evidence/fix-violations-unit.log` (diagnostics, scene-content, contract and templates tests: 46 pass, `eslint` clean). `evidence/acceptance-fix-2-inspect.log` is the helper over all nine steps: all settled, 0 advisory warnings, and step 1 shows the text and icon."},{"line":2591,"text":"- **Integration or end-to-end regression assessment:** the browser-backed inspection suite already runs the helper on controlled presentations. A browser test of the new check would need a fixture whose entities paint late, which cannot be made to happen reliably. The pure function is unit-tested on exactly those sample shapes, so I added no new browser test. If the next round still sees a blank first capture, the new `UNSETTLED` line should name the entities, which would show the real cause."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-39e9c8951c6e9f7a (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":2328,"end_line":2330,"lines":[{"line":2328,"text":"## Visual and client evidence"},{"line":2329,"text":""},{"line":2330,"text":"Round 2 screenshot metadata and text equivalents are in `acceptance-screenshots/README.md`; captures are `acceptance-screenshots/round-2/root-step-01.png` and `bootstrap-step-01.png`. The bootstrap capture shows starter scene text while settled. verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":2585,"end_line":2591,"lines":[{"line":2585,"text":"## Round 1 finding A-002: the inspection helper reported a settled first step whose scene text was missing"},{"line":2586,"text":"- **Question:** the tester reports two helper runs where `step-01.png` showed the `prompt` and `you` outlines without their text or icon, while the log said `step 1/9 ... settled` and `0 advisory warnings`. Is that a defect, and what is the cause?"},{"line":2587,"text":"- **Requirement:** `presentation-verification`, \"Visual inspection artifacts\" and \"Screenshots are settled\": the helper waits for transitions to settle before each screenshot. `presentation-skill`, \"Self-verify before reporting completion\": the visual check uses settled screenshots."},{"line":2588,"text":"- **Ruling:** the symptom could not be reproduced, but the helper's settled check was weaker than its claim, so I hardened it. Evidence for the first part: I ran the helper five times at the default 1500 ms settle, including three runs with every core busy, and every `step-01.png` was byte-identical (md5 `03e51f0b…`) and showed the text and icon. The tester's own preserved screenshots, `sample-wide-step-01-helper-default.png` and `sample-wide-step-01-helper-3000.png`, are byte-identical to that capture and also show the text and icon. The blank capture itself was not preserved. The old check only looked at the `Appear` and scene wrapper opacities, so it could not notice a first load whose entities were not yet painted, whatever the cause. Step 1 has no entry transition, which also explains why only the first capture was affected. I ruled this a real weakness in the \"settled\" claim, not a runtime defect: the sample renders its entities correctly."},{"line":2589,"text":"- **Change:** before each screenshot the helper now also waits for fonts to load, then takes two samples of every entity two animation frames and 100 ms apart. A step counts as settled only when no entity moved or resized by more than 0.5 px, faded, appeared or disappeared between the samples. It retries for up to 5 s. If it still is not settled, it prints the existing `UNSETTLED` line and a warning that names up to three affected entities. An entity that is steady but deliberately dimmed or hidden counts as settled, and elements sharing one entity id are keyed by DOM order so each is compared with itself. The helper script and its library were copied unchanged into the bootstrap template, so the parity contract still holds. The kit and the sample are untouched."},{"line":2590,"text":"- **Regression coverage:** new unit tests of `unsettledEntities` in `tests/unit/inspect-diagnostics.test.ts` (steady; moving, resizing, fading, appearing or disappearing entities; steady dimmed or hidden entities) and of `collectSceneContent` in `tests/unit/inspect-scene-content.test.ts` (duplicate ids, accumulated opacity). Output: `evidence/acceptance-fix-2-unit.log` and, after validator review changes, `evidence/fix-violations-unit.log` (diagnostics, scene-content, contract and templates tests: 46 pass, `eslint` clean). `evidence/acceptance-fix-2-inspect.log` is the helper over all nine steps: all settled, 0 advisory warnings, and step 1 shows the text and icon."},{"line":2591,"text":"- **Integration or end-to-end regression assessment:** the browser-backed inspection suite already runs the helper on controlled presentations. A browser test of the new check would need a fixture whose entities paint late, which cannot be made to happen reliably. The pure function is unit-tested on exactly those sample shapes, so I added no new browser test. If the next round still sees a blank first capture, the new `UNSETTLED` line should name the entities, which would show the real cause."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-39e9c8951c6e9f7a (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":2328,"end_line":2330,"lines":[{"line":2328,"text":"## Visual and client evidence"},{"line":2329,"text":""},{"line":2330,"text":"Round 2 screenshot metadata and text equivalents are in `acceptance-screenshots/README.md`; captures are `acceptance-screenshots/round-2/root-step-01.png` and `bootstrap-step-01.png`. Both are 1280×720 captures from production previews. Compare the root capture with round 1's default-helper blank capture to see A-002's resolution. The bootstrap capture shows starter scene text while settled. Rounds 1 and 2 retested the fixed seams at narrow and wide sizes, in present mode, and in the bootstrap helper. The skill conversation, scaffold and create/modify journeys were not exercised. The record says this is because no agent-skill runner or interactive answer channel was available. The rubric names exactly this kind of gap as environmental, so it does not count against coverage. These are optional surfaces and a small share of the behavior; the default attribution, the brand slot and the typed sample payload were all exercised. One scenario was observed only weakly: continuing entities not fading as newcomers was checked through DOM persistence and position, not opacity. That is a single scenario inside an otherwise well-exercised motion requirement. It is neither a significant undisclosed omission nor a substantial share of the behavior the environment allowed.
